back2basics.concept: Supreme Court Collegium and Judicial Appointments
back2basics.text: The Supreme Court Collegium is a body of senior Supreme Court judges led by the Chief Justice of India that recommends appointments and transfers of judges in the higher judiciary. Its recommendations are crucial for maintaining judicial independence and are followed by the government as per the Memorandum of Procedure. The Collegium system ensures a consultative process among judges for judicial appointments.

2026-11-26-am-3816692751.deck: The Supreme Court Collegium recommended Justice Vibhu Bakhru as the next Chief Justice of Jharkhand High Court days before the incumbent's retirement. This highlights the judicial appointment process and the role of the Collegium system, important for understanding judiciary functioning in India.

back2basics.concept: Foreign Exchange Reserves and Their Management
back2basics.text: Foreign exchange reserves are assets held by a country's central bank in foreign currencies, used to back liabilities and influence monetary policy. Managing these reserves involves maintaining adequate levels to support the currency, meet external obligations, and ensure economic stability. Transparency in reporting reserve status helps build trust among investors and supports effective economic governance.

2026-11-26-am-3c931db14b.deck: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) published its 47th half-yearly report on the management of foreign exchange reserves for April to September 2026, showing an increase in reserves. This report highlights RBI's commitment to transparency in managing the country's foreign exchange reserves, a key aspect for economic stability and policy formulation.

body.label: Udyam Assist Platform

back2basics.concept: Parliamentary Consultative Committees and PRAGATI platform
back2basics.text: Parliamentary Consultative Committees are forums where ministers and members of parliament discuss policies and programmes of ministries, enhancing parliamentary oversight and accountability. PRAGATI is a governance platform that integrates central and state governments to monitor and resolve implementation challenges in projects and schemes, promoting timely and quality execution.

2026-11-26-am-721fcec271.deck: On 25 November 2026, the Union Education Minister chaired the Parliamentary Consultative Committee meeting focused on the internationalisation of Indian education, highlighting initiatives to expand India's educational footprint globally. On the same day, the Prime Minister chaired the 55th PRAGATI meeting reviewing major infrastructure projects and the Industrial Training Institute ecosystem to improve governance and skill development.

body: Parliamentary Consultative Committees facilitate dialogue between ministers and MPs to review policies and programmes, ensuring parliamentary oversight.
The PRAGATI platform integrates central and state governments to monitor project implementation, address bottlenecks, and ensure timely delivery.
Examples include the Education Ministry's Consultative Committee meeting on internationalisation of education and the PM's review of infrastructure projects and ITI ecosystem under PRAGATI.
These mechanisms promote transparency, coordination, and responsiveness in governance.
structure.conclusion: Together, these platforms strengthen democratic accountability and improve policy implementation in India.
structure.intro: Parliamentary Consultative Committees and PRAGATI are mechanisms to improve governance and accountability in India.

mcq.trap: Statement 1 is correct but must note it includes academic collaborations and attracting international students, not only campuses; Statement 2 correctly describes PRAGATI's role.

body.label: Committee meeting details
body.text: The Union Education Minister chaired the first Parliamentary Consultative Committee meeting of 2026 for the Ministry of Education, attended by senior ministry officials and MPs.

body.label: Global footprint expansion
body.text: The Ministry aims to expand the global footprint of the Indian Knowledge System by setting up campuses of Indian Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) overseas and facilitating foreign universities to establish campuses in India.

body.label: Current foreign HEIs and collaborations
body.text: Around 21 foreign HEIs operate in India, alongside joint academic and research collaborations.

body.label: Four strategies for internationalisation
body.text: The Department of Higher Education promotes internationalisation through academic and research collaborations, attracting international students, allowing foreign HEIs to set up branch campuses in India, and enabling Indian HEIs to establish campuses abroad.

body.label: Key initiatives and regulations
body.text: Seventeen Letters of Intent have been issued to foreign universities from countries like the UK, USA, Australia, and Italy under UGC regulations; initiatives like Bharat Innovates, SPARC, GIAN, DASA, and the revamped Study in India portal support this effort.

body.label: School education internationalisation
body.text: 268 CBSE schools operate in 26 countries with a regional office in Dubai; curriculum alignment with global standards, multilingual education, exchange programs, and a standardised assessment framework support internationalisation.

body.label: Policy guidance
body.text: The National Education Policy 2020 and the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047 guide transformative shifts in Indian education towards internationalisation.

sections.heading: What initiatives were discussed for internationalising Indian education?

body.label: PRAGATI platform purpose
body.text: PRAGATI is an ICT-enabled, multi-modal platform that brings together Central and State Governments to address implementation bottlenecks and improve delivery of projects and welfare schemes.

body.label: Infrastructure projects reviewed
body.text: The Prime Minister reviewed five critical infrastructure projects in road, power, coal, and railway sectors worth over ₹78,000 crore.

body.label: Emphasis on timely execution
body.text: The PM stressed that delays in infrastructure projects cause cost escalation and postpone benefits, urging ministries and states to resolve issues with clear responsibility and realistic timelines.

body.label: Quality and rehabilitation focus
body.text: Timely execution must be accompanied by high construction quality; rehabilitation and resettlement in coal projects should be dignified and timely.

body.label: Innovative power projects
body.text: The PM suggested exploring decentralised solar and wind power projects closer to consumption centres to improve reliability and ease transmission pressure.

body.label: ITI ecosystem and PM-SETU
body.text: The PM reviewed the Industrial Training Institute ecosystem and the Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation through Upgraded ITIs (PM-SETU), calling for stronger PSU–ITI linkages and industry participation.

body.label: 3C approach for ITIs
body.text: The PM advocated the Classroom–Company–Career (3C) approach linking classroom learning, practical industry experience, and employment to enhance skill development and job opportunities.

body.label: Local employment and migration
body.text: Stronger links between ITIs and local employers can expand employment closer to home, reducing distress-driven migration and aiding regional economic development.

back2basics.text: The Consumer Price Index (CPI) measures the average change over time in the prices paid by consumers for a market basket of goods and services. Inflation refers to the rate at which the general level of prices for goods and services rises, eroding purchasing power. The RBI targets inflation within a tolerance band to maintain price stability while supporting growth.

2026-11-26-am-84ecfb2eb1.deck: The Reserve Bank of India’s November 2026 Bulletin reports that headline CPI inflation rose to 6.1% in October 2026, driven mainly by broad-based increases in food prices. back2basics.text: A passport is an official document issued by the government certifying a person's identity and citizenship, allowing international travel. The Regional Passport Office verifies documents before issuing passports. Administrative justice requires that any action such as impounding a passport must follow due process, including clear communication of allegations and reasonable time for response. The judiciary plays a role in reviewing such administrative actions to ensure fairness and legality.

2026-11-26-am-d624204c14.deck: Saurav Das, co-convenor of the Cockroach Janata Party, was stopped from boarding a flight at Delhi airport due to a show-cause notice from the Chennai Regional Passport Office alleging discrepancies in his passport documents. This incident raises questions on passport verification procedures and administrative actions affecting judicial figures, relevant for understanding separation of powers and administrative justice.

body.label: Notice timing
body.text: Saurav Das received an email notice at 7:30 p.m. on November 23, 2026, just hours before his scheduled 1 a.m. flight to London, about alleged discrepancies in his passport.

body.label: Reason for stopping
body.text: The Chennai Regional Passport Office alleged that particulars such as place of birth in his passport application were incorrect and that the passport was obtained by material suppression of facts.

body.label: Outcome
body.text: Das was stopped from boarding the flight at the immigration counter due to failure to respond satisfactorily to the notice.

sections.heading: What happened with Saurav Das at the Delhi airport?

body.label: Due process concerns
body.text: Das argued that the notice was received only hours before travel and that no details of the alleged discrepancies were disclosed before stopping him, raising questions on procedural fairness.

body.label: Judicial implications
body.text: Das is the Chief Justice of Punjab & Haryana High Court, and the incident followed a Madras High Court order on a PIL seeking investigation into his nationality and passport validity.

body.label: Freedom of movement
body.text: Stopping a judicial figure from international travel on such grounds touches upon rights related to freedom of movement and administrative accountability.

sections.heading: Why does this matter for administrative justice and legal rights?

body.label: Madras High Court PIL
body.text: A Public Interest Litigation petition filed in Madras High Court sought a probe by the Ministry of Home Affairs into Das's nationality and requested cancellation of his passport and Aadhaar if found not Indian.

body.label: Court order
body.text: The Madras High Court ordered notice to Das and directed investigation into alleged discrepancies in his documents.

sections.heading: What background legal actions led to this notice?

body.label: Political context
body.text: Das is associated with the Cockroach Janata Party, a youth movement critical of the government, which he alleges is using administrative tactics to suppress dissent.

body.label: Allegations of censorship
body.text: Das claimed government attempts to stop him from speaking at prestigious universities abroad and alleged mass censorship on social media platforms.
